issues.reason: The standing half is that *Propositional attitudes* requires a speech verb's finite clausal complement to be sealed under `Theme` and none is emitted; the overstated half is the repair it implies, since every clause of the quote is negated and the registered limitation states a seal 'has no polarity carrier … seal what is expressible and leave the negated conjunct out; this is a registered limitation, not a licence to assert the positive form', while non-factive `say` bars asserting P at top level — so no negated seeing, negated granting, or `So` atom can be emitted anywhere.

The definite-projection rule projects a definite's typing atom *beside the wrapper*; with no wrapper emitted, `(Member sk_urgency_1 urgency)` stands alone as a free-standing assertion that an urgency exists — precisely what the quoted speaker denies and what the text nowhere states, i.e. over-assertion per the calibration line.

The strandedness half stands (nothing predicates of the witness, a consequence of the unsealable complement), but the claim that 'this' and 'it' are necessarily separate referents is refuted — *Coreference & anaphora* resolves an anaphor to the most salient compatible antecedent, and 'I don't see the urgency in this so I'm not going to grant it' most naturally has both point at the same request.
